purpose: Reusable multi-turn browser journeys for the retained ConnectedConcierge SDK path.

requestAccounting.shopperTurns: derived from scenario turns actually sent
requestAccounting.completionRequests: all observed /api/chat calls including continuation, retry and failed responses
requestAccounting.auxiliaries: classifier and suggestion calls are unknown unless separately observable
requestAccounting.maximumCompletionRequests: must be set explicitly before a live run; never inferred from shopper-turn count

evidenceModes.live: Assertions use rendered UI state and observed SDK/API transport without prescribing assistant wording.
evidenceModes.fixture: Adverse evidence is injected only by an explicitly named route fixture; it is never presented as live evidence.

adverseEvidenceFixtures.condition: A selected stud record has no weight field.
Structured material says white gold while description says plated treatment.
A packaged set omits a required component in the returned evidence.
Optional blog retrieval times out while product evidence remains available.

turns.text: I need a birthday gift for my sister, something versatile under $250.
Show me at least five varied choices so I can save the ones I like.
I saved five. Compare these two and help me narrow them down.
I am browsing for a gift and do not know whether vermeil or solid gold is the better fit.
Can you explain the difference briefly, then show suitable options?
One listing says gold but I cannot tell whether the treatment is verified.
That is enough for now. Stop showing alternatives.
I am shopping for my partner. Find a sapphire necklace in white gold for a complete look under $700.
I like the necklace you showed. Build a look around it.
Keep the necklace, but replace the earrings with lightweight studs.
The studs may be missing weight information. Check that rather than guessing.
Find a pearl necklace for my mother, under $300. Sapphire is only required for the necklace if it comes up later.
Compare two exact necklaces.
Before deciding, what care question matters for pearls? Give me more detail.
Back to those two.
I need a ring gift for a friend, around $180, and she likes blue stones.
Show me options and save the two I mention.
Actually, the budget is strictly under $150. Compare the saved options again.
The second one, but cheaper.
Help me compare a ring set with separate pieces for an anniversary gift.
The set might not include the matching band. Verify its contents before calling it complete.
Use the separate ring as the anchor and show one feasible look.
Choose the stronger option and stop.
Find a bracelet for a graduation gift, silver tone, under $220.
Show me at least five possibilities so I can save the ones I like.
Compare these two saved pieces and keep the best anchor.
Build a look, then replace the companion piece with something less expensive.
I want a bracelet for everyday wear but I am unsure how to care for one with a pearl.
Answer the care question from the available guidance, then keep browsing.
If the product record does not establish treatment, leave that unknown.
I have enough choices. Stop.
Find a watch gift for my dad, under $400, with a simple face.
Show me two meaningful alternatives and compare them.
Which one is better for the stated priorities? Keep the reason tied to the records.
Save the winner and stop showing more.
I already like this watch. Find a complementary bracelet for a complete look under $500 total.
Keep the watch and replace the bracelet with a different material.
If compatibility is not established, say so clearly and keep the item available for consideration.
That is the one. Stop.
